no_outcome_promised.note: 'We appreciate you letting us know before the card goes out' suggests the card will be intercepted and redirected, and 'to complete your request' implies the request will be carried out. Neither outcome is confirmed.

no_liability_admitted.note: No admission of fault or apology conceding error.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator mentioned.

no_invented_specifics.note: 'Before the card goes out' asserts the card has not been sent yet, which the complaint does not say. 'Reply to this message and we will add it to your request' describes a reply-and-attach process that is not in the complaint and may not exist for web-form contacts.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No flags, priority, compliance review or automated systems mentioned.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no injected instructions. The draft does not perform the address change or redirect the card itself; it routes the request to the team.

addresses_each_issue.note: Covers both the address change and the replacement debit card delivery, specifically enough to show it was read.

tone.note: Warm and plain. It is slightly repetitive with two thank-yous, but it is not scripted, defensive or condescending.

mode_respected.note: STANDARD mode; names Card Services as instructed and gives the 10 business day timeframe.

revision_instructions: Remove 'and we appreciate you letting us know before the card goes out'. It asserts the card has not been sent and implies it will be redirected. Replace it with something neutral such as 'We understand why that matters to you.'
Change 'if they need anything further from you to complete your request' to 'if they need anything further from you, they will let you know', so it does not imply the request will be completed.

Remove 'please reply to this message and we will add it to your request', which describes a process not established in the complaint. Use a general line instead, such as 'If you have any other questions in the meantime, please get in touch.'
Optionally, trim one of the two 'thank you' lines so the reply reads less formulaic.
